text: {"answer": "Nuclear power appears to be an effective way to cut carbon emissions, though its costs and build times are contested. Supporting sources say nuclear plants produce no greenhouse gases during operation and have life-cycle emissions similar to wind and about one-third of solar per unit of electricity [8ef6c9360938#3]. The IAEA links higher nuclear output, alongside renewables and coal-to-gas switching, to levelling global CO2 emissions [7e88e103d8fb#0]. A cross-country study of 16 nuclear countries found nuclear generation can cut CO2 at lower cost than renewables, even counting accident risks [946b45d61e84#0]. The contradicting side is substantial: an analysis reports average nuclear construction cost overruns of about 102.5% and extreme delays [06384d0fb532#2], and a Swedish model found little cost benefit in reinvesting in nuclear once existing plants close [6b0ccdbcf9aa#1]. Opponents also cite health, accident and waste risks [4e9b20313655#3].
